newsitem.title: USA: Clinton renews appeal to Senate to back treaty.
newsitem.headline: Clinton renews appeal to Senate to back treaty.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton renewed an appeal to the Republican-led Senate Friday to ratify a global chemical weapons treaty, saying the United States "should stand with those who want to destroy chemical weapons."

"The bottom line is this: Will the United States join a treaty we helped to shape or will we go from leading the fight against poison gas to the list of pariah nations" outside the treaty, he told reporters.
Clinton used a hastily called news conference to lobby for Senate ratification next week of the Chemical Weapons Convention, which goes into force on April 29, with or without U.S. participation.
The treaty, already ratified by more than 70 countries, bars development, production, stockpiling, transfer and use of chemical weapons.

Clinton denied that his decision to reorganize the State Department was aimed at appeasing conservative Republican Sen. Jesse Helms of North Carolina, the chief critic of the treaty, in hopes of getting him to approve it. Clinton said he did not think he could get Helms to change his mind.

"America should stand with those who want to destroy chemical weapons, not with those who defy the international community. I urge every member of the Senate to support the convention when it comes to a vote next week," he said.
